newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Yield Spreads-Curve finally flattens.
newsitem.headline: Australia Yield Spreads-Curve finally flattens.

text.p: The sharp steepening in the Australian bond yield curve seen since the surprise official interest rate cut on May 23 came to a halt on Monday as the short-end finally succumbed to profit-taking, traders said.
The three/10-year bond futures spread had put on nearly 30 basis points since the policy easing to 5.5 percent.
However, Stephen Roberts, chief economist at UBS Australia, believes the pullback will be short-lived with the short-end remaining well protected by the lower cash rate.

"Three bonds still offer close to 75 basis points over cash and in the near term that may compress to around 60 basis points over cash and drive the 3-10 year spread consistently above 120 basis points," Roberts said.
The local market also lost ground against the U.S. after its recent strong outperformance as the market prepared itself for Wednesday's first quarter GDP.
The U.S. rallied on Friday on continued foreign buying and amid hopes that the economy will continue to show modest growth.
The domestic market was mixed against Canada ahead of today's Canadian election, while the New Zealand market was closed for the Queen's Birthday holiday.
